transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's just... well, what brings me in is that I'm just so exhausted lately. And I know everyone gets tired, especially working full-time, but this feels different. It's like a tiredness that sleep doesn't really fix, you know? Even just getting through a normal workday at the office and then coming home to make dinner... it just feels so much heavier than it should. I'm still getting everything done, of course, I don't want to sound like I'm not functioning, but it's just taking a lot more effort. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way—when did this exhaustion first start?

Um, well... I think it's been about a month now. It's a bit strange, actually, because right before this started, I was doing really, really well. I had all this energy and was just incredibly driven at work—getting my whole team organized, staying on top of absolutely everything. I felt fantastic, honestly. 

But then it just... well, it swung the other way, into this persistent slump where I'm just so low and tired all the time. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making a big deal out of nothing, because I know everyone has their ups and downs. Does that sound like a normal kind of shift to you? To just drop like that and be down for a month after a really productive streak?
Before this exhaustion started, how many days in a row did that period of high energy and drive last?

Oh, gosh, um... I'm actually not entirely sure. I'm so sorry, I probably should have paid closer attention so I could give you a better answer. I didn't really count the exact days. 

It was just... a really nice, productive stretch. Maybe a few days? Or maybe a week? I'm not completely certain. I just remember feeling really capable and getting everyone at work on track, which was great for the team. I hope it's alright that I don't have a precise number for you. Is it okay if I'm a little fuzzy on the exact timeline? I just didn't think to track it at the time since I was just feeling so good.
During that week or so when you were feeling so energetic and productive, did you notice you needed less sleep than usual but still felt rested?

Um, well... yes, actually. I hope that doesn't sound too strange or, you know, unhealthy. But... yeah, I really didn't need much sleep at all then. I think I was only getting, oh, maybe four hours a night? 

But I honestly felt completely fine! I wasn't dragging or anything. I'd wake up and just feel so ready to go—sending out work emails, sketching out some event ideas, or even reorganizing the whole kitchen before anyone else was even awake. It felt like a good thing at the time, just... being really efficient and making the most of the day. Is it okay to have a stretch like that where your body just doesn't seem to need as much rest?
During this past month of low energy and exhaustion, have you had any thoughts of hopelessness, worthlessness, or thoughts of harming yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I've had any thoughts of harming myself or anything like that. I really want to be clear about that. But... I guess, as far as feeling worthless... maybe a little bit? 

I hope this doesn't sound too dramatic, but I just... I keep replaying things in my head lately. Like, every time I've had to cancel a family plan because I was just too exhausted, or every time I've been a bit short with my husband. It just makes me feel like I'm really letting everyone down, you know? Like I'm not doing a good enough job as a wife, or a mother, or even as a manager at work right now. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I'm really trying not to be. I just feel bad that I can't be as present for them as I usually am. Does that make sense? Is it normal to feel that kind of guilt when you're just going through a low patch like this?

During this past month, has your low energy and exhaustion affected your ability to keep up with your usual responsibilities—like going to work or managing daily tasks—or have you still been able to get everything done, even if it's harder?

Um, well, I'm definitely still going to work and taking care of things at home. I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up or letting everything fall apart, because I'm not. I'm trying really hard to keep everything going. 

But... I guess I'd have to admit it's been a little harder than usual. I've been a bit slower at making decisions at work, which isn't like me. And like I mentioned, I've had to back out of a few family plans, which I feel terrible about. I've also sort of stepped back from my art projects... usually I love painting and sketching, but I just haven't had the energy for it lately. 

I'm still getting the important things done, though! I promise I am. It just takes a lot more effort right now. Is that okay? I mean, is it understandable that I'm just moving a little slower while I'm feeling this way?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a distinct manic/hypomanic period (~1 week) with elevated energy, decreased need for sleep (4 hours, felt rested), increased goal-directed activity, and heightened productivity, followed by a switch into a current depressive episode lasting about one month characterized by persistent fatigue, low mood, guilt/worthlessness, decreased interest in pleasurable activities (painting), psychomotor slowing, and mild functional impairment (withdrawing from family plans, slower decision-making) without suicidal ideation. The clear history of a prior hypomanic/manic episode followed by a depressive episode meeting moderate severity criteria supports a diagnosis of Bipolar affective disorder, current episode moderate depression (F31.3), rather than unipolar major depressive disorder (F33.1) or a purely hypomanic presentation (F31.81).
